blocks.text: Why a Chauffeur Makes Sense in Anaheim
Three practical reasons, specific to this city.
blocks.html: Three practical reasons, specific to this city.

items: Disney and the Convention Center both sell out their own parking early in the day, so a pre-booked coach eliminates the paid-park-and-shuttle routine.
Disney's fireworks and Angels game endings create synchronized traffic surges that are much easier to ride out in a vehicle with a driver.
Venues span the full width of the city from Disneyland west to Honda Center east, roughly 8-10 miles apart, so multi-stop days need ground transport.
I-5 and SR 57 through Anaheim are the most congested corridors in Orange County at peak hours.

blocks.text: We also quote Anaheim to the hour rather than the trip. Most groups need four hours, and four is the standard minimum across the industry because a committed vehicle cannot be sold to anyone else while it is parked at your venue. If your night genuinely needs less, ask for a one-way transfer rate instead of paying a full minimum.

blocks.text: Choosing a Vehicle for a Anaheim Night

Capacity is the first filter, then cost per person. A stretch limo seats 6 to 8, a Chrysler 300 about 8, a Hummer 12, and a Sprinter limo up to 14. Our party bus seats 24. Below about ten people, two cars or a limo usually beats a bus. Above ten, the bus wins on cost per head and nobody gets left behind.

blocks.text: Licensed, Insured, and Backup Plans

Every chauffeur on our team is licensed and background checked, and our vehicles are licensed and inspected. Our drivers work the night and do not drink, which matters when the group includes teenagers, and we set a fixed return time off the venue's posted close so nobody is standing in a parking lot at 1 AM wondering where the car went.

blocks.text: Booking, Minimums, and What Is Not Included

Send us four things and we will put a fixed number in writing: your date and start time, how many passengers and how many are under 18, your pickup address or ZIP, and how many stops. Most Anaheim groups find a four-hour minimum covers the night comfortably.

The driver stays with the group. There is no waiting fee for parked hours.
